name: Chest press
description: A supported press to learn a steady pushing movement.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest. Keep your feet flat and your back against the pad.
steps: Hold the handles with wrists straight.
Press forward without locking your elbows.
Return slowly until your elbows are just behind your body.
feel: You should feel your chest working, with help from the front of your shoulders and the backs of your arms.
common: Keep your shoulders relaxed. Start with a weight you can move smoothly for every repetition.

name: Lat pulldown
description: A guided pull that helps you learn to use your back.
setup: Set the thigh pad snugly over your legs. Sit tall and take the bar a little wider than shoulder width.
steps: Start with arms long and chest comfortably lifted.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest.
Let the bar travel upward slowly without shrugging.
feel: The sides of your back should do most of the work. Your arms assist the pull.
common: Bring the bar in front of you, not behind your neck. Avoid swinging your torso.

name: Leg press
description: A stable way to practise a controlled lower-body push.
setup: Sit fully into the backrest. Place your feet around shoulder width on the platform and check the safety stops before starting.
steps: Release the safety handles with the platform controlled.
Lower until your knees bend comfortably.
Push through the whole foot and stop before your knees lock.
feel: Your thighs and glutes should share the effort. Keep your lower back supported.
common: Use a comfortable range. Do not let your knees collapse inward or bounce at the bottom.

name: Seated cable row
description: A seated pull for your back with room to focus on posture.
setup: Sit tall with feet on the supports and knees slightly bent. Hold the handle with arms extended.
steps: Keep your chest easy and shoulders down.
Draw the handle toward your lower ribs.
Extend your arms slowly while staying tall.
feel: Think of your shoulder blades moving gently toward each other. Your arms will help.
common: Avoid leaning far back or rounding your shoulders at the start.

name: Seated leg curl
description: A simple machine for learning the back-of-leg movement.
setup: Align the machine pivot with your knee. Place the lower pad just above your heels and adjust the thigh pad to hold you comfortably.
steps: Hold the handles and sit against the backrest.
Curl the pad down and back smoothly.
Return slowly without letting the weight stack crash.
feel: You should feel the backs of your thighs working through the motion.
common: Keep your hips on the seat and use a light weight while you learn the setup.

name: Shoulder press
description: A seated press to practise pushing overhead with support.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles begin around shoulder height. Keep your back against the pad and feet planted.
steps: Grip the handles without bending your wrists.
Press upward in a comfortable path.
Lower slowly until your hands return near shoulder level.
feel: The front and side of your shoulders help drive the press, with your triceps assisting.
common: Stay in a pain-free range. Do not force the handles lower than feels comfortable.
